title: Sunny Deol Has Never Made a Netflix Film. Akshaye Khanna Hasn't Faced Him in Thirty Years. That Changes Thursday.
excerpt: Ikka reunites two of Bollywood's most magnetic actors in a courtroom thriller that asks what happens when the best lawyer in the country is forced to defend a man he knows is guilty. Streaming globally on Netflix, July 10.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Sunny Deol makes his Netflix debut with 'Ikka' on July 10.
  • Deol and Akshaye Khanna reunite on screen after 32 years.
  • The film explores moral dilemmas in a courtroom setting.
  • Tillotama Shome plays a pivotal role as a public prosecutor.
  • Director Siddharth P. Malhotra emphasizes emotional depth in storytelling.
Bollywood's Dynamic Duo Returns
›Debuts July 10, 2026 Sunny Deol's first Netflix film: 'Ikka'
›Last film together: 1994 First collaboration with Akshaye Khanna in 32 years
›Known for the line: 'We fight for what's right' Deol plays Arjun Mehra, a principled defense attorney
›Defended by Mehra, who knows his guilt Khanna portrays Shauryaman Gaur, a murder suspect
https://x.com/NetflixIndia/status/2074757883808407778 He hasn't done this in thirty-two years. Not the courtroom — **Sunny Deol** has returned to that set plenty of times since *Damini* made "tarikh pe tarikh" a national catchphrase. What he hasn't done, until now, is show up on a streaming platform. **Ikka**, premiering on Netflix this Thursday, July 10, is Sunny Deol's first-ever Netflix original. And the man they've put opposite him makes it worth the wait. https://youtube.com/watch?v=unf8x_aZg9Y ![Sunny Deol — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/d/d9/Sunny_Paaji_2024.jpg) > **"It begins to belong to the people who breathe life into it." — Director Siddharth P."** **Akshaye Khanna** reunites with Deol on screen for the first time in nearly three decades, and their pairing here is the kind of casting decision that makes you lean forward before the trailer even finishes. Deol plays **Arjun Mehra**, a celebrated defence attorney whose principles have never bent — a man who declares, in the film's best line, *"Hum court mein jeetne ke liye nahi, haq ke liye ladte hai"* (We don't fight to win in court; we fight for what's right). Khanna plays **Shauryaman Gaur**, the murder suspect Mehra is forced to defend — a man whose downfall Mehra himself was once responsible for. > "Every film begins with a script. Words on paper. Ideas waiting to be discovered. But somewhere along the journey, the film stops belonging to the writer or the director. It begins to belong to the people who breathe life into it." — Director Siddharth P. Malhotra The setup is a pressure cooker. Arjun is blackmailed into a "life for a life" deal to protect his family, forced to use every legal loophole to free a man he knows is guilty. It's a psychological chess match dressed in courtroom procedure, and the trailer suggests director **Siddharth P. Malhotra** knows exactly how to tighten the screws. But the women in this film may be its secret weapon. **Tillotama Shome** plays Madhura Banerjee, a ruthless public prosecutor determined to secure a conviction — and in a genre dominated by male posturing, her presence promises something sharper. "She is one of those rare artists who elevates every frame simply by being in it," Malhotra wrote in an emotional tribute to his cast days before the premiere. **Dia Mirza** rounds out the core cast as Avantika, Arjun's wife, trying to hold her family together while her husband's moral universe collapses around him. **Sanjeeda Sheikh** plays Shauryaman's wife, and the supporting cast — **Shishir Sharma**, **Akansha Ranjan Kapoor**, **Vijay Vikram Singh** — adds further depth to a story that refuses to offer easy answers. Malhotra, in a remarkably candid series of posts ahead of the premiere, described calling **Sanjeeda Sheikh** close to midnight and asking if she could shoot the next day. Her response: *"You're directing it? I'm coming."* That's the kind of trust a director earns — or bluffs. ![Akshaye Khanna — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7f/Akshaye_Khanna_at_the_launch_of_GUJCON_CRF_and_PRF.jpg) Music comes from **Julius Packiam** (score) and **Mithoon** (songs), a pairing that suggests emotional depth alongside legal tension. The screenplay, by **Althea Kaushal** and **Mayank Tewari**, is built around the question every great courtroom drama eventually asks: what happens when justice and truth point in different directions?
Supporting Cast Strengthens the Narrative
›Promises a sharp performance Tillotama Shome as ruthless prosecutor
›Holds family together amid chaos Dia Mirza plays Avantika, Arjun's wife
›Adds depth to the story Sanjeeda Sheikh as Shauryaman's wife
›Trust built through collaboration Director praises Shome's elevating presence
## Where to Watch **Ikka** premieres globally on **Netflix** on **July 10, 2026** — available everywhere Netflix streams, which means NRIs in the US, UK, Canada, and beyond can watch it the moment it drops. No theatrical window, no geo-blocking. Hindi language, with subtitles expected in multiple languages. For Sunny Deol fans in the diaspora who've been watching his streaming-era peers — Akshay Kumar on Prime, Ajay Devgn on JioHotstar — this is his Netflix debut, and the pairing with Akshaye Khanna gives it an electricity that a solo vehicle wouldn't have. Two actors who've aged into very different kinds of screen presence, forced into the same frame for the first time in a generation. This Thursday. Set a reminder.
